# Cam Link Pro

> Blender 4.x/5.x add-on. Receives a live 6DOF camera pose (position +
> rotation + focal length + sensor width) over the network from a
> companion Android AR app, drives a target Camera object with it in
> real time, records takes to keyframes, and mixes takes on the NLA. A
> second TCP channel streams a live JPEG monitor of the driven camera's
> view back to the sender and accepts remote record commands.

This file is a compact, structured reference for an AI assistant
working with this add-on or its companion phone app's source. It states
facts and exact identifiers rather than narrative explanation — see
`README.md` in this same directory for the human-readable walkthrough.

## System shape

Two halves, communicating over two independent connections on the same
LAN:

- **This add-on** (`cam_link_pro/`, Blender-side): a UDP receiver for
  pose data, a TCP server for video+commands, an NLA baking/mixing
  workflow, and a sidebar panel.
- **A companion phone app** (Unity + AR Foundation, Android; not part
  of this package): reads AR tracking, runs a pose-processing pipeline,
  sends UDP pose packets, and opens the TCP video/command connection.
  Its spec and reference C# source may exist alongside this add-on in a
  sibling project (`PoseMath.cs`, `CamLinkTrackerDriver.cs`,
  `CamLinkClient.cs`, `CAMLINK_APP_SPEC.md`) — if you're asked about
  that side of the system and those files aren't in front of you, say
  so rather than guessing at Unity/AR Foundation specifics.

Do not assume the phone app exists or is reachable when reasoning about
this add-on in isolation — every wire contract below is the *complete*
interface between the two; nothing else is shared (no filesystem, no
shared process, no other side channel).

## File map

- `__init__.py` — `bl_info`, `CamLinkProSettings` (PropertyGroup on
  `Scene.cam_link_pro`), all operators, `VIEW3D_PT_cam_link_pro` panel,
  `WM_OT_camera_stream_server` (the UDP modal server — this is the
  core loop, see below).
- `video_channel.py` — `VideoCommandServer` (TCP accept/read/write
  threads + two queues), `capture_frame_jpeg()` (main-thread-only
  OpenGL viewport capture → JPEG bytes), pairing string/QR helpers,
  `local_lan_ip()`.
- `qr_gen.py` — dependency-free QR matrix + PNG encoder.
- `README.md` — human-facing docs.
- `llms.txt` — this file.

## Wire contracts (exact, do not paraphrase when implementing against these)

### Pose (UDP, phone → Blender)
One packet per pose update, fire-and-forget, no ack/retry.
```
sequence_id,pos_x,pos_y,pos_z,rot_x,rot_y,rot_z,focal_length_mm,sensor_width_mm
```
- 9 comma-separated ASCII fields, no spaces.
- `sequence_id`: non-negative int, monotonically increasing for the
  life of the connection (not restarted at reconnect). Receiver drops
  any packet whose id is `< last_packet_id` applied
  (`WM_OT_camera_stream_server.last_packet_id`).
- `pos_x/y/z`: metres, already Blender space (right-handed, Z-up).
- `rot_x/y/z`: degrees, already Blender's default XYZ Euler order
  (`R = Rz · Ry · Rx`).
- `focal_length_mm`, `sensor_width_mm`: floats.
- Receiver: `WM_OT_camera_stream_server._parse_packet()` /
  `_drain_and_apply()`. Malformed lines (wrong field count, non-numeric)
  are silently dropped, never raised.
- Default port `5005`, configurable via `settings.port`.

### Video + command (TCP, both directions)
Single persistent connection, port `5006` default
(`settings.video_port`).
- On connect, client's first line: `AUTH <token>\n` — must match
  `settings.pairing_token`, else the connection is otherwise unusable
  (no video, no accepted commands — see `_handle_line`, which silently
  ignores anything before/besides the recognized command set; there is
  no explicit auth rejection response, an unauthenticated client just
  never gets anything back).
- Inbound commands (newline-terminated ASCII): `START`, `STOP`, `PING`.
  Anything else is ignored, not errored. (`LOCK_START` used to be valid
  here too, back when the phone had a "Lock Start" toggle; that feature
  was removed from the phone app, so `LOCK_START` is no longer recognized
  and `is_armed`/`ARMED` are gone entirely.)
- Outbound status lines: `REC_ON`, `REC_OFF`, `REMOTE_DISABLED`, `PONG`,
  and `STATE <token>` (see below). `REMOTE_DISABLED` is sent in place of
  silently ignoring a `START`/`STOP` when `remote_control_enabled` is
  off, so the phone has something to react to instead of a no-op Record
  tap -- this is a new addition to the wire contract (coordinate with
  the phone app before relying on it there).
- `STATE <token>\n` — `<token>` is exactly one of `CONNECTED` (streaming,
  not live), `LIVE_NODATA` (live, no pose packet in the last
  `POSE_TIMEOUT_S` = 1.5s), or `LIVE` (live and receiving) — computed by
  the shared `_live_state_token()` helper, the same one the panel's
  traffic light uses, so the two can never disagree. There is
  deliberately no `DISCONNECTED` token: that state is already fully
  conveyed by the TCP connection itself dropping. Sent from
  `_drain_commands` (main thread only — never from `_accept_loop`/
  `_client_reader` in `video_channel.py`, which run on background
  threads and must not touch `settings.*`/`bpy`), on two independent
  triggers, checked every tick regardless of `is_live`: (1) the token
  changed since the last one sent (`self._last_sent_state`), or (2)
  `video_server.client_count` increased since last tick
  (`self._last_client_count`) — this second trigger is what lets a
  phone that reconnects mid-session to an already-live, already-steady
  Blender learn the current state immediately rather than wait for the
  next transition that may never come. Not gated by
  `remote_control_enabled` or `video_enabled` (mirrors
  `phone_connected`/`pose_receiving`). No `STATE` line is sent from
  `_finish()` on Disconnect — the socket closing is itself the signal.
- Outbound video frames, interleaved with status lines on the same
  socket: 4-byte big-endian unsigned length prefix, then exactly that
  many bytes of JPEG. Distinguish by peeking the first byte (status
  lines start with a printable ASCII character; a length prefix's
  first byte is `0` for any realistic frame size).
- `remote_control_enabled` gates whether `START`/`STOP` from the phone
  are honored (a `START`/`STOP` dropped for this reason sends
  `REMOTE_DISABLED` back); `PING` is always honored.
- `STOP` while `is_recording` only flips `is_recording` off and sends
  `REC_OFF` — it deliberately does **not** auto-bake to NLA. An earlier
  version called `bpy.ops.anim.cam_link_bake_to_nla()` here so a
  phone-stopped take couldn't end up as a "dangling" unbaked Action;
  that was removed because it committed the take to an NLA strip under
  whatever `active_take_name`/`take_blend_type` happened to already be
  set, with no chance to review first. Stopping from the phone and
  stopping from the panel toggle now behave identically either way:
  the take sits as a plain active Action until `anim.cam_link_bake_to_nla`
  is invoked explicitly (panel button or scripted).

### Pairing QR
```
camlink://<ip>:<pose_port>:<video_port>?t=<token>
```
Generated by `WM_OT_camlink_show_qr` via
`video_channel.pairing_qr_png_bytes()`, written to a temp PNG and
opened with the OS's default viewer (`bpy.ops.wm.path_open`).

## `CamLinkProSettings` (PropertyGroup, `context.scene.cam_link_pro`)

| Property | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ip_address` | str | `"0.0.0.0"` | UDP bind interface |
| `port` | int | `5005` | UDP pose port |
| `target_camera` | Object (CAMERA poll) | none | driven camera; falls back to `scene.camera` |
| `smoothing_factor` | float 0–1 | `0.8` | lerp factor, `current = current*f + incoming*(1-f)` |
| `drive_location` | bool | `True` | gate: live stream (and Record Motion's keyframe_insert) writes X/Y/Z |
| `drive_rotation` | bool | `True` | gate: live stream (and Record Motion's keyframe_insert) writes rotation_euler |
| `is_streaming` | bool | `False` | sockets open (Connect/Disconnect) -- independent of whether the camera is driven |
| `is_live` | bool | `False` | connected stream is actually driving the camera + recording allowed (Start/Stop Live Stream). Requires `is_streaming` |
| `phone_connected` | bool | `False` | read-only, set every tick from `video_server.client_count > 0`. Only ever True if `video_enabled` was on at Connect time (that's what starts the TCP video/command server at all), but the panel now shows this status regardless of the current `video_enabled` toggle state |
| `phone_client_count` | int | `0` | read-only, set every tick from `video_server.client_count` (already authenticated-only). Same `video_enabled`-at-Connect caveat as `phone_connected`. Panel shows a warning if this is `> 1` |
| `pose_receiving` | bool | `False` | read-only, set every tick: a valid pose packet parsed within the last `WM_OT_camera_stream_server.POSE_TIMEOUT_S` (1.5s) — decays, doesn't require a packet on the exact current tick |
| `is_recording` | bool | `False` | currently baking live values to keyframes |
| `active_take_name` | str | `"Take_01"` | name for next NLA bake |
| `take_blend_type` | enum | `REPLACE` | `REPLACE`\|`ADD`\|`SUBTRACT`\|`MULTIPLY`\|`COMBINE` — `NlaStrip.blend_type` used by the next bake |
| `video_port` | int | `5006` | TCP video/command port |
| `video_enabled` | bool | `False` | run the JPEG monitor stream |
| `video_fps` | int 5–30 | `15` | capture throttle, independent of the 60Hz pose tick |
| `remote_control_enabled` | bool | `True` | honor phone `START`/`STOP` |
| `pairing_token` | str | `""` (generated on demand -- both by the panel on first draw and by the Connect/QR operators) | required `AUTH` value |

## Operators

| bl_idname | Class | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `wm.camera_stream_server` | `WM_OT_camera_stream_server` | Connect/Disconnect. Modal: opens UDP socket (+ TCP video server if enabled), 60Hz timer (`TIMER_INTERVAL = 1/60`), resets `is_live`/`phone_connected`/`pose_receiving` to False on connect. Drains/tracks pose every tick regardless of `is_live` (for status); only writes to the camera and allows recording when `is_live` is True. `_finish()` (disconnect) also forces `is_live`/`phone_connected`/`pose_receiving` back to False |
| `wm.cam_link_toggle_live` | `WM_OT_camlink_toggle_live` | Start/Stop Live Stream. Non-modal, touches no socket -- just flips `is_live`; refuses (`CANCELLED`) if `is_streaming` is False. Turning live off also forces `is_recording` False |
| `anim.cam_link_bake_to_nla` | `ANIM_OT_bake_take_to_nla` | pushes the active Action (object transform + camera-data lens/sensor_width) into new NLA track(s) named `active_take_name`, blend type = `take_blend_type`, extrapolation `NOTHING`; clears the active action afterward |
| `anim.cam_link_setup_delta_rig` | `ANIM_OT_camlink_setup_delta_rig` | see *Delta rig* below |
| `wm.cam_link_new_token` | `WM_OT_camlink_new_token` | regenerates `pairing_token` |
| `wm.cam_link_show_qr` | `WM_OT_camlink_show_qr` | writes + opens the pairing QR PNG |

## The 60Hz apply loop (`_drain_and_apply`), exact order

1. Drain the UDP socket fully (non-blocking); keep only the newest
   datagram this tick — older ones in the same tick are discarded
   unread.
2. Parse the newest payload (or `None` if nothing arrived this tick).
3. **Regardless of `is_live`:** if parsed successfully, stamp
   `self.last_packet_wall_time = time.time()`. Every tick (parsed or
   not), set `settings.pose_receiving = (now - last_packet_wall_time) <
   POSE_TIMEOUT_S` (1.5s) — this is why Pose Receiving already reflects
   real data before you ever go live. If nothing parsed, return here.
4. Drop on `seq_id < last_packet_id`.
5. Lerp `current_loc`/`current_rot_deg`/`current_focal`/
   `current_sensor_width` toward the incoming values by
   `smoothing_factor`. **This also runs regardless of `is_live`** — the
   smoothing baseline stays warm while merely Connected, so the first
   frame after going Live isn't a jump from a stale value.
6. **If not `is_live`: return here.** Nothing below this line runs
   unless the stream is live — Connect alone can never move the camera
   or record.
7. **If `drive_location`:** write `cam_obj.location.x/y/z` from the
   lerped position. **If `drive_rotation`:** write
   `cam_obj.rotation_euler` (degrees → radians) from the lerped
   rotation. These are direct RNA property writes — they always win
   over whatever an Action/NLA stack on the *same object* evaluated to
   that redraw; there is no live "additive" mode for a single object
   (see *Known limitation* below).
8. Always write `cam_obj.data.lens` and `cam_obj.data.sensor_width`
   from the lerped focal/sensor values (no gate for these — only
   location/rotation are gated, and only while live).
9. If `is_recording`: `_insert_keyframes()` — keys only the channels
   `drive_location`/`drive_rotation` currently allow, always keys
   `lens`/`sensor_width`, then advances `scene.frame_current` by 1.

`_drain_commands` separately sets `settings.phone_connected =
video_server.client_count > 0` and `settings.phone_client_count =
video_server.client_count` every tick it runs (independent of
`is_live`). Its `START` handler requires `remote_control_enabled` (else
`REMOTE_DISABLED` is sent back) and, separately, `is_live` (silently
ignored, no status line — merely Connected isn't enough to record even
with remote control allowed). `STOP` only checks `remote_control_enabled`
(same `REMOTE_DISABLED` reply if off).

`invoke()` seeds `current_loc`/`current_rot_deg` from the target
camera's *actual current* `.location`/`.rotation_euler` at the moment
streaming starts (evaluated value, e.g. from any existing animation on
that frame) — not from Delta Transform, which is a separate matrix
component this add-on never reads or writes.

## Known limitation: no live "additive on the same object"

"Add on top of an existing animation" is fundamentally an NLA/
playback-time concept (`NlaStrip.blend_type`). The live 60Hz loop above
always does an absolute RNA write, which is evaluated *after* any
animation on that object for that redraw — so a hand-keyed or NLA'd
animation on the *same* object the stream is driving will always be
overwritten/fought with live, regardless of what blend type you later
set on a baked NLA strip. Setting `take_blend_type = ADD` only affects
how a *finished, baked* take composites during scene playback — it
does not make the live stream itself additive, and does not give a
correct WYSIWYG preview while recording.

**The supported fix is `anim.cam_link_setup_delta_rig`**, not the
`ADD` blend type: it splits the base animation onto a new parent Empty
(created at the camera's current world transform, so nothing jumps),
moves the camera's existing Action onto that Empty, resets the camera
to `(0,0,0)` local, and parents the camera to the Empty. Ordinary
Blender parent→child transform composition then combines the Empty's
independently-evaluated base animation with the camera's live-driven
local delta every frame — correctly, live, in the monitor preview, and
while recording — because the add-on is no longer writing to the same
object that carries the base animation.

Preconditions enforced by the operator (returns `{'CANCELLED'}`
otherwise, with a `self.report({'ERROR'}, ...)` explaining why):
target camera must exist and be type `CAMERA`; must have no existing
parent; must have no existing NLA tracks (both cases are left for
manual setup rather than risked being reshuffled automatically).

**Blender 4.4+ "layered actions" gotcha**, load-bearing if you ever
touch this operator's action-moving code or write similar code
elsewhere in this add-on: reassigning `some_id.animation_data.action =
existing_action` alone is **not sufficient** to make it evaluate for
the new owner — the new "layered" action model resolves channels by
`AnimData.action_slot`, not by which ID happens to reference the
action. Without also carrying `action_slot` across (or assigning one of
`action.slots`), the target evaluates as if unanimated — frozen at
whatever static value the properties held, with no runtime error. This
is the same reason `ANIM_OT_bake_take_to_nla._push_down` guards
`strip.action_slot` when pushing to NLA. Verified against Blender
5.2.1 LTS via an isolated `--background` script;
`bpy.types.Action.fcurves` does not exist directly in this API
generation either — fcurves live under
`action.layers[].strips[].channelbags[<slot>].fcurves`.

## Known bug + fix: monitor capture JPEG failure

Symptom: repeating console spam
`Video monitor error: bpy_struct: item.attr = val: enum "JPEG" not
found in ('FFMPEG')`, with `video_enabled` auto-flipping to `False`
each time.

Cause: `capture_frame_jpeg()` sets
`scene.render.image_settings.file_format = "JPEG"` to grab a still.
Blender 4.0+ added `ImageFormatSettings.media_type` (`IMAGE` \|
`MULTI_LAYER_IMAGE` \| `VIDEO`); when a scene's output is configured for
video, `file_format`'s own enum dynamically shrinks to just `FFMPEG`,
so the JPEG assignment raises. Reproduced directly against Blender
5.2.1: setting `media_type = 'VIDEO'` then `file_format = 'JPEG'`
raises exactly this error; setting `media_type = 'IMAGE'` first makes
it succeed.

Fix (present as of this version): `capture_frame_jpeg()` now saves
`media_type` (via `hasattr` guard for older Blender without the
property), forces it to `IMAGE` before setting `file_format`, and
restores it in the `finally` block — restoring `media_type` *before*
`file_format`, since the previous `file_format` value may not be legal
under the previous `media_type` until both are put back in the right
order.

If this error still appears after updating the source file on disk:
Python already has the old module loaded in the running Blender
process; editing `.py` files does not hot-reload a running add-on.
Toggle the add-on off/on in Preferences, or restart Blender.

## FAQ: "why does the scene appear to move when I move the phone?"

Almost always expected behavior, not a bug — check before assuming
otherwise:

1. **If you're watching through the driven camera** (Camera View, or
   the phone's own JPEG monitor overlay), every static object will
   appear to shift/rotate opposite to the camera's motion. That is
   optically identical to a real handheld camera: turn your head right
   and the room visually slides left across your field of view — the
   room never moved, you're just viewing from inside the moving
   element. This is inherent to first-person camera footage, not
   specific to this add-on.
2. **To confirm the camera really is independent:** switch to an
   outside 3D viewport (not Camera View — orbit around freely) and
   watch the camera object/frustum icon itself glide around while other
   objects (a Cube, a Light, etc.) sit still. If that's what you see,
   everything is working correctly — the earlier "the world spins"
   feeling was purely the first-person perspective effect in (1).
3. **If, from that outside view, other objects genuinely move or
   rotate together with the camera** (not just the camera itself),
   that's a real issue, and the most likely cause is accidental
   parenting: check the Outliner for anything nested under the
   Camera object or under a rig Empty (e.g. one created by
   `anim.cam_link_setup_delta_rig`) — this add-on only ever writes to
   the single Target Camera object, so anything else moving must be
   parented (directly or transitively) to something that is.
4. Unrelated to either of the above: "Reset Origin" on the phone and
   any Delta Transform set on the Blender camera are two independent
   concepts that never interact — Reset Origin only changes what
   numbers the phone computes before sending; it has no knowledge of,
   and never touches, anything inside the Blender file.

## Explicitly out of scope for this add-on

- No iOS support anywhere in this system (the phone app is
  Android/ARCore-only by design).
- No reliability/retry layer on the pose UDP channel — packet loss is
  intentionally invisible (next packet just arrives late).
- This add-on must never be asked to modify the phone app's wire
  contracts (pose packet shape, command set, QR string format) — those
  are fixed by design; a phone-side change would break pairing without
  a matching Blender-side change, and vice versa.
